title: The Mole and Stoichiometry
seo_title: Chemistry 11: The Mole and Stoichiometry Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: The mole is a quantity used to make atoms and molecules measurable: Avogadro's number, molar mass, percent composition and empirical formulas, stoichiometry, limiting reactant and percent yield. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Chemistry 11)
meta_desc: Free Chemistry 11 worksheets (BC Curriculum): the mole and stoichiometry. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Use mole ratios from the balanced equation.
body_html:
How to think about it

A mole is 6.02 × 10²³ particles (Avogadro's number). Molar mass (g/mol) is the mass of one mole: n = m ÷ M. Percent composition and empirical formulas come from the masses of the elements in a compound.

Stoichiometry uses the coefficients of a balanced equation as mole ratios: grams → moles → mole ratio → moles → grams. The limiting reactant runs out first and decides how much product forms; percent yield = actual ÷ theoretical × 100%.

Example

How many moles are in 36 g of water (M = 18 g/mol)?

n = m ÷ M

Answer: 2 mol

Example

2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. How many mol of water form from 3 mol O₂?

Ratio 1 : 2

Answer: 6 mol

Common mistakes

  • Using grams instead of moles in the mole ratio.
  • Choosing the reactant with the smaller mass as limiting.
  • Forgetting to balance the equation first.

faq.a: Atoms are too small to count, so a mole links the number of particles to a mass we can weigh.

faq.q: Why is percent yield usually below 100%?
faq.a: Some product is lost, reactions may be incomplete, and side reactions happen.

items.q: How many particles (molecules or formula units) are in 2 mol of calcium carbonate (CaCO<sub>3</sub>)?
A sample has 3.01 × 10<sup>24</sup> particles of aluminum oxide (Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>). How many moles is that?
A sample has 1.81 × 10<sup>24</sup> particles of nitrogen gas (N<sub>2</sub>). How many moles is that?
How many moles of atoms in total are in 4 mol of sucrose (C<sub>12</sub>H<sub>22</sub>O<sub>11</sub>)?
items.e: Each formula has 45 atoms, so 4 × 45 = 180 mol.

items.q: How many particles (molecules or formula units) are in 1.5 mol of sodium carbonate (Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>)?
How many particles (molecules or formula units) are in 4 mol of calcium chloride (CaCl<sub>2</sub>)?

How many moles of O atoms are in 3 mol of calcium carbonate (CaCO<sub>3</sub>)?
items.e: Each formula has 3 O, so 3 × 3 = 9 mol.

items.q: How many moles of Cl atoms are in 3 mol of magnesium chloride (MgCl<sub>2</sub>)?
items.e: Each formula has 2 Cl, so 3 × 2 = 6 mol.

items.q: How many moles of O atoms are in 1 mol of sodium carbonate (Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>)?
items.e: Each formula has 3 O, so 1 × 3 = 3 mol.

items.q: How many moles of atoms in total are in 2 mol of aluminum oxide (Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>)?
items.e: Each formula has 5 atoms, so 2 × 5 = 10 mol.

items.q: How many moles of O atoms are in 4 mol of aluminum oxide (Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>)?
items.e: Each formula has 3 O, so 4 × 3 = 12 mol.

items.q: Who stated the law of conservation of mass?
items.e: Matter is neither created nor destroyed in a reaction.

items.q: How many particles (molecules or formula units) are in 4 mol of nitric acid (HNO<sub>3</sub>)?
Equal volumes of all gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules. Whose law is this?
Which law says gases react in simple whole-number ratios by volume?
items.e: 2 volumes of H₂ + 1 volume of O₂ → 2 volumes of steam.

items.q: How many molecules or formula units are in 1.20 g of CH<sub>4</sub>? (N<sub>A</sub> = 6.02 × 10<sup>23</sup> mol⁻¹)

Calculate the mass of 0.050 mol of C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub>.

A compound contains C 24.3%, H 4.00%, Cl 71.7% by mass. What is its empirical formula?
items.e: Divide each % by A<sub>r</sub>, then divide by the smallest: C 2.02, H 4.00, Cl 2.02.

items.q: A compound contains 52.9% Al, 47.1% O by mass. What is its empirical formula? (Ar: Al = 27, O = 16)
items.e: Divide each mass (or %) by Ar, then divide by the smallest number to get the simplest whole-number ratio: Al₂O₃.

items.q: A compound contains 112 g of Fe, 48 g of O. What is its empirical formula? (Ar: Fe = 56, O = 16)
items.e: Divide each mass (or %) by Ar, then divide by the smallest number to get the simplest whole-number ratio: Fe₂O₃.

items.q: Calculate the molar mass (in g mol⁻¹) of C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub>.
What is the SI unit of the amount of substance?
A compound contains 6 g of C, 1 g of H. What is its empirical formula? (Ar: C = 12, H = 1)
items.e: Divide each mass (or %) by Ar, then divide by the smallest number to get the simplest whole-number ratio: CH₂.

items.q: A compound has the empirical formula C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub>O and molar mass = 184. What is its molecular formula?
items.e: M<sub>r</sub> of C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub>O = 46.0; 184 ÷ 46.0 = 4, so multiply by 4.

items.q: What percent of the mass of glucose (C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub>) is H? (H = 1, C = 12, O = 16; molar mass = 180 g/mol)
A compound contains 2.4 g of C, 0.8 g of H. What is its empirical formula? (Ar: C = 12, H = 1)
items.e: Divide each mass (or %) by Ar, then divide by the smallest number to get the simplest whole-number ratio: CH₄.

items.q: A compound contains C 40.0%, H 6.70%, O 53.3% by mass. What is its empirical formula?
items.e: Divide each % by A<sub>r</sub>, then divide by the smallest: C 3.33, H 6.70, O 3.33.

items.q: What percent of the mass of potassium chloride (KCl) is Cl? (Cl = 35.5, K = 39; molar mass = 74.5 g/mol)
What percent of the mass of sodium chloride (NaCl) is Na? (Na = 23, Cl = 35.5; molar mass = 58.5 g/mol)
A compound contains 6 g of C, 1.5 g of H. What is its empirical formula? (Ar: C = 12, H = 1)
items.e: Divide each mass (or %) by Ar, then divide by the smallest number to get the simplest whole-number ratio: CH₃.

items.q: What percent of the mass of carbon dioxide (CO<sub>2</sub>) is O? (C = 12, O = 16; molar mass = 44 g/mol)
What percent of the mass of copper(II) sulfate (CuSO<sub>4</sub>) is O? (O = 16, S = 32, Cu = 63.5; molar mass = 159.5 g/mol)
A compound contains 54 g of Al, 48 g of O. What is its empirical formula? (Ar: Al = 27, O = 16)
items.e: Divide each mass (or %) by Ar, then divide by the smallest number to get the simplest whole-number ratio: Al₂O₃.

items.q: What percent of the mass of ethanol (C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub>O) is H? (H = 1, C = 12, O = 16; molar mass = 46 g/mol)
Calculate the molar mass (in g mol⁻¹) of CaCO<sub>3</sub>.
A compound contains 128 g of Cu, 16 g of O. What is its empirical formula? (Ar: Cu = 64, O = 16)
items.e: Divide each mass (or %) by Ar, then divide by the smallest number to get the simplest whole-number ratio: Cu₂O.

items.q: What percent of the mass of nitric acid (HNO<sub>3</sub>) is N? (H = 1, N = 14, O = 16; molar mass = 63 g/mol)

When an acid is neutralized: H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> + 2NaOH → Na<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> + 2H<sub>2</sub>O. What mass of Na<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> form from 40 g of NaOH? (NaOH = 40 g/mol, Na<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> = 142 g/mol)

When glucose is used in respiration: C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub> + 6O<sub>2</sub> → 6CO<sub>2</sub> + 6H<sub>2</sub>O. What is the mole ratio of O<sub>2</sub> to C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub>?
When magnesium burns: 2Mg + O<sub>2</sub> → 2MgO. What is the mole ratio of Mg to O<sub>2</sub>?
When ethane burns: 2C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub> + 7O<sub>2</sub> → 4CO<sub>2</sub> + 6H<sub>2</sub>O. What is the mole ratio of O<sub>2</sub> to H<sub>2</sub>O?
When nitrogen oxide forms in an engine: N<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2NO. What is the mole ratio of O<sub>2</sub> to NO?
When propane burns in a grill: C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub> + 5O<sub>2</sub> → 3CO<sub>2</sub> + 4H<sub>2</sub>O. What is the mole ratio of H<sub>2</sub>O to O<sub>2</sub>?
When iron rusts: 4Fe + 3O<sub>2</sub> → 2Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>. How many moles of O<sub>2</sub> react with 3 mol of Fe?
items.e: 3 mol Fe × (3 mol O<sub>2</sub> ÷ 4 mol Fe) = 2.25 mol.

items.q: When hydrogen peroxide decomposes: 2H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> → 2H<sub>2</sub>O + O<sub>2</sub>. What is the mole ratio of H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> to O<sub>2</sub>?

When an acid is neutralized: H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> + 2NaOH → Na<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> + 2H<sub>2</sub>O. What mass of H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> is needed to make 54 g of H<sub>2</sub>O? (H<sub>2</sub>O = 18 g/mol, H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> = 98 g/mol)
When aluminum reacts with acid: 2Al + 6HCl → 2AlCl<sub>3</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub>. What is the mole ratio of H<sub>2</sub> to AlCl<sub>3</sub>?
When aluminum reacts with oxygen: 4Al + 3O<sub>2</sub> → 2Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>. What is the mole ratio of O<sub>2</sub> to Al?
When propane burns in a grill: C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub> + 5O<sub>2</sub> → 3CO<sub>2</sub> + 4H<sub>2</sub>O. How many moles of H<sub>2</sub>O form along with 3 mol of CO<sub>2</sub>?
items.e: 3 mol CO<sub>2</sub> × (4 mol H<sub>2</sub>O ÷ 3 mol CO<sub>2</sub>) = 4 mol.

items.q: When methane burns: CH<sub>4</sub> + 2O<sub>2</sub> → CO<sub>2</sub> + 2H<sub>2</sub>O. What is the mole ratio of H<sub>2</sub>O to CO<sub>2</sub>?
When nitrogen oxide forms in an engine: N<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2NO. What is the mole ratio of NO to O<sub>2</sub>?
When iron rusts: 4Fe + 3O<sub>2</sub> → 2Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>. How many moles of Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> form from 8 mol of Fe?
items.e: 8 mol Fe × (2 mol Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> ÷ 4 mol Fe) = 4 mol.

items.q: When propane burns in a grill: C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub> + 5O<sub>2</sub> → 3CO<sub>2</sub> + 4H<sub>2</sub>O. How many moles of CO<sub>2</sub> form from 4 mol of O<sub>2</sub>?
items.e: 4 mol O<sub>2</sub> × (3 mol CO<sub>2</sub> ÷ 5 mol O<sub>2</sub>) = 2.4 mol.

items.q: When aluminum reacts with acid: 2Al + 6HCl → 2AlCl<sub>3</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub>. What mass of Al react with 18.25 g of HCl? (HCl = 36.5 g/mol, Al = 27 g/mol)
When potassium chlorate decomposes: 2KClO<sub>3</sub> → 2KCl + 3O<sub>2</sub>. What is the mole ratio of KClO<sub>3</sub> to O<sub>2</sub>?
When sulfur dioxide is oxidized: 2SO<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2SO<sub>3</sub>. What is the mole ratio of O<sub>2</sub> to SO<sub>3</sub>?
When propane burns in a grill: C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub> + 5O<sub>2</sub> → 3CO<sub>2</sub> + 4H<sub>2</sub>O. What is the mole ratio of H<sub>2</sub>O to CO<sub>2</sub>?

When glucose is used in respiration: C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub> + 6O<sub>2</sub> → 6CO<sub>2</sub> + 6H<sub>2</sub>O. You start with 4 mol of C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub> and 8 mol of O<sub>2</sub>. Which is the limiting reactant?
items.e: The equation needs C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub> : O<sub>2</sub> = 1 : 6; 4 mol C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub> ÷ 1 = 4, 8 mol O<sub>2</sub> ÷ 6 = 1.33. The smaller one runs out first.

items.q: When magnesium burns: 2Mg + O<sub>2</sub> → 2MgO. You start with 10 mol of Mg and 1 mol of O<sub>2</sub>. Which is the limiting reactant?
items.e: The equation needs Mg : O<sub>2</sub> = 2 : 1; 10 mol Mg ÷ 2 = 5, 1 mol O<sub>2</sub> ÷ 1 = 1. The smaller one runs out first.

items.q: When sulfur dioxide is oxidized: 2SO<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2SO<sub>3</sub>. You start with 2 mol of SO<sub>2</sub> and 12 mol of O<sub>2</sub>. How many moles of SO<sub>3</sub> can form?
items.e: SO<sub>2</sub> is limiting; it gives 2 mol of SO<sub>3</sub>.

items.q: Ethan's calculation says 50 g of iron should form, but only 30 g is collected. What is the percent yield?
5.00 g of Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> gave 1.57 g of Fe (Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO<sub>2</sub>). Calculate the percentage yield.
When hydrogen burns in oxygen: 2H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2H<sub>2</sub>O. You start with 2 mol of H<sub>2</sub> and 10 mol of O<sub>2</sub>. How many moles of H<sub>2</sub>O can form?
items.e: H<sub>2</sub> is limiting; it gives 2 mol of H<sub>2</sub>O.

items.q: The theoretical yield of aspirin is 80 g. Benjamin gets a yield of 75%. What mass does Benjamin collect?
20.0 mL of 0.20 mol/L KOH was neutralized by 15.2 mL of H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>. Calculate the concentration of the H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>.
items.e: n(KOH) = 0.00400 mol; ratio acid : base = 1 : 2, so n(H2SO4) = 0.00200 mol; c = n/V = 0.132 mol/L.

items.q: Ava's calculation says 50 g of sodium chloride should form, but only 37.5 g is collected. What is the percent yield?
Sofia's calculation says 200 g of sodium chloride should form, but only 140 g is collected. What is the percent yield?
Priya's calculation says 50 g of copper should form, but only 40 g is collected. What is the percent yield?

When propane burns in a grill: C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub> + 5O<sub>2</sub> → 3CO<sub>2</sub> + 4H<sub>2</sub>O. You start with 8 mol of C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub> and 6 mol of O<sub>2</sub>. How many moles of CO<sub>2</sub> can form?
items.e: O<sub>2</sub> is limiting; it gives 3.6 mol of CO<sub>2</sub>.

items.q: The theoretical yield of calcium carbonate is 80 g. Nathan gets a yield of 85%. What mass does Nathan collect?
The theoretical yield of sodium chloride is 100 g. Kai gets a yield of 75%. What mass does Kai collect?
50.0 g of N<sub>2</sub> reacts completely: N<sub>2</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub> → 2NH<sub>3</sub>. Calculate the maximum (theoretical) mass of NH<sub>3</sub>.
items.e: n(N2) = 1.79 mol, n(NH3) = 3.57 mol, m = 60.7 g.

items.q: Calculate the percentage atom economy for making Fe by this reaction: Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO<sub>2</sub>.
items.e: Atom economy = Mr of desired product ÷ total Mr of reactants × 100 = 111.6 ÷ 243.6 × 100 = 45.8%.

items.q: When ammonia is made from nitrogen and hydrogen: N<sub>2</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub> → 2NH<sub>3</sub>. You start with 10 mol of N<sub>2</sub> and 1 mol of H<sub>2</sub>. Which is the limiting reactant?
items.e: The equation needs N<sub>2</sub> : H<sub>2</sub> = 1 : 3; 10 mol N<sub>2</sub> ÷ 1 = 10, 1 mol H<sub>2</sub> ÷ 3 = 0.33. The smaller one runs out first.

items.q: When hydrogen burns in oxygen: 2H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2H<sub>2</sub>O. You start with 8 mol of H<sub>2</sub> and 3 mol of O<sub>2</sub>. Which is the limiting reactant?
items.e: The equation needs H<sub>2</sub> : O<sub>2</sub> = 2 : 1; 8 mol H<sub>2</sub> ÷ 2 = 4, 3 mol O<sub>2</sub> ÷ 1 = 3. The smaller one runs out first.

items.q: 25.0 mL of 0.20 mol/L Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub> was neutralized by 23.5 mL of HCl. Calculate the concentration of the HCl.
items.e: n(Na2CO3) = 0.00500 mol; ratio acid : base = 1 : 1/2, so n(HCl) = 0.0100 mol; c = n/V = 0.426 mol/L.

items.q: When sodium reacts with chlorine: 2Na + Cl<sub>2</sub> → 2NaCl. You start with 2 mol of Na and 12 mol of Cl<sub>2</sub>. How many moles of NaCl can form?
items.e: Na is limiting; it gives 2 mol of NaCl.
